title: Preserve the ordinary spill under an existing competing owner
question: Does an ordinary drain before the next spill recover the original admission boundary of a wider merge?
summary: At 96 initial runs, the same 536,788,041-byte peer allows the ordinary next spill. Both the wider spill and an immediate ordinary drain are denied.

workloads: 96 tiny spill runs followed by one buffered record, fixed 256 MiB job and 512 MiB pool.

validation.summary: The successful path verifies all 97 rows. Both denied paths return typed shared errors and clear temporary files and reservations.

limitations: An injected peer tests early resource overlap in the feature-free Linux sorter.
exclusions: Production input parsing and complete-job elapsed time.
reopen_when: Show that the pending-run and optional fallback owners fit before the spill writer starts, then preserve late sink admission separately.
